game.tickets: $1 Hot Spot only + $2 base+Bulls-Eye on the same numbers

engines.name: RANDOM
engines.method: Uniform random baseline — the honest control group.

engines.name: HOT
engines.method: Top frequency in the window. Chasing streaks — mathematically identical odds to any other pick.

engines.name: GAP
engines.method: Longest current drought since last appearance.

engines.name: CLUSTER
engines.method: Grows one contiguous blob. Seeds on the hottest 6-draw cell, then repeatedly annexes whichever adjacent cell has the strongest recent heat — so the ticket is always a connected shape like the 21-22-23-24-25 run you saw.

engines.name: BLOCK
engines.method: Best 2-wide rectangle — two adjacent columns stacked over several rows, like the 8/9-18/19-28/29-38/39 slab. Scores every position on the grid and plays the hottest block.

engines.name: MARKOV
engines.method: First-order transition model. For each candidate, sums P(candidate next | ball b was just drawn) across all 20 balls of the last draw, using the full co-occurrence matrix from your log.

engines.name: PATTERN
engines.method: The only engine that learns. Online logistic model over 10 signals — lag-1/2/3 carryover, pair affinity with the last draw, row/column momentum, own-gap dueness, short-window burst. Weights update after every draw, so it is genuinely reading the log, not just frequency.

engines.name: DEVIATION
engines.method: Pure statistics, no carryover. Each ball gets a shrunk z-score against the binomial expectation (25% per draw) in three windows at once — last 30, last 90, whole log — weighted 50/30/20, with a 1.3x boost when all three agree in sign. That is the only thing a genuinely biased machine looks like: the same balls over-represented at every timescale, not just since the last draw. The ticket is then grown greedily with a co-occurrence penalty, so it never stacks five balls that always travel together — the hits stay statistically independent and the variance drops.

clustering.note: Touching pairs = side-by-side or stacked on the 10x8 grid. 142 adjacent cell pairs exist.

predictionLedger.note: Threshold scales with ticket size: alertAt(spot) = max(3, round(spot/4) + 2). Compare thresholdRate to thresholdRateByChance, never to a fixed 8.4%.
